speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes. To understand what is causing these symptoms, I need to know how long this jaundice has been present and if you have noticed any abdominal pain, nausea, or changes in your urine or stool color.

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B infection with acute liver failure.

The patient's age, history of high-risk sexual behavior, and acute onset of jaundice with agitation strongly suggest a viral hepatitis, specifically Hepatitis B. Cocaine and alcohol use can exacerbate liver injury, but the rapid progression to encephalopathy (agitation) indicates severe hepatic dysfunction. Given the high stakes, I will proceed with specific serological testing to confirm the etiology and assess liver synthetic function immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_surface_antigen, Hepatitis_B_core_IGM, Liver_function_panel, PT/INR, Ammonia_level.
